The first print is binding, with no correction-day grace period."},{"kind":"tool","tool":"official.lookup","call":"Fetch the USDA FNS SNAP national monthly participation table and read the latest FY2026 Persons observations.","result":"The table dated June 12, 2026 reports 38,456,892 persons in January 2026, 37,729,410 in February 2026, and 37,298,271 in March 2026, equivalent to 38.456892, 37.729410, and 37.298271 million."},{"kind":"tool","tool":"official.lookup","call":"Fetch the same official SNAP table's recent reference-class history.","result":"Official Persons values were 42,180,523 in February 2025, 42,193,855 in March, 42,353,149 in April, 42,248,301 in May, 42,084,880 in June, 42,012,830 in July, 41,836,900 in August, and 41,633,090 in September."},{"kind":"tool","tool":"official.lookup","call":"Check the official SNAP table's FY2026 transition and annual summaries.","result":"Persons fell from 41,091,800 in October 2025 to 39,997,940 in November and 39,205,146 in December; USDA reports FY2025 average participation of 42,383,194 and the preliminary FY2026-to-date average of 38,963,243."},{"kind":"tool","tool":"official.lookup","call":"Verify release timing against the official FNS program-data schedule and target release window.","result":"The official schedule places the June 2026 SNAP monthly-table release on 2026-11-03; the latest table available during this run covered March 2026 and was dated 2026-06-12."},{"kind":"text","text":"The outside-view base rate is persistence with drift for a slowly moving administrative caseload. The 13 monthly changes from February 2025 through March 2026 average -0.376 million, while October 2025 through March 2026 participation fell 3.794 million. The level anchor is therefore March's 37.298 million; momentum remains negative, with the smaller March decline supporting partial moderation."},{"kind":"text","text":"Mechanisms are separated into the March level, recent downward momentum, moderation as declines decelerate, and a negative adjustment for tighter eligibility and work-rule mechanisms. Administrative reporting volatility remains a secondary source of uncertainty."},{"kind":"math","text":"Prior/update/interval: persistence-with-drift prior anchored at March 2026 = 37.298271 million. Apply momentum of -0.580 million per month for April-June (-1.740), moderation of +0.100 million per month (+0.300), and a policy-mechanism adjustment of -0.308, for a net update of -1.748 and point = 37.298 - 1.748 = 35.550 million. The historical sample is 13 successive monthly changes from February 2025 through March 2026 in the official table; vintage status for every historical observation is not separately identified. Its sample standard deviation is sigma = 0.376 million. The one-month 80% half-width is 1.28*sigma = 1.28*0.376 = 0.482 million; scaling over three months gives 0.482*sqrt(3) = 0.835, rounded to 0.840. Final implied bounds are 35.550 +/- 0.840 = [34.710, 36.390]."},{"kind":"text","text":"Upside risk: faster stabilization in enrollment or delayed implementation of tighter eligibility rules would land above 36.39 million. Downside risk: an average decline greater than about 0.863 million per month from March through June, broad recertification losses, or unusually aggressive enforcement would put June below 34.71 million, outside the interval."},{"kind":"text","text":"Review disposition: Accepted the correction from FNA to USDA FNS and expanded the prior/update calculation to show the anchor, momentum, moderation, policy adjustment, volatility scaling, and bounds. Also clarified that the historical table does not separately establish first-print vintage status and quantified the downside path."},{"kind":"forecast","point":35.55,"ciLow":34.71,"ciHigh":36.39}]}
